people.sub: The claimed Dulce security officer. Confessed as an invention by the man who says he invented him
people.narrative: THE NAME WAS CONFESSED AS AN INVENTION BY THE MAN WHO SAYS HE INVENTED IT. Thomas Edwin Castello is presented in the Dulce literature as a security technician who worked inside the alleged facility, stole a set of photographs and papers, and vanished with his family. In November 2015 Tal Levesque, who wrote under the name Jason Bishop III and who authored the two original Dulce Base articles, told the researcher Adam Gorightly by email: 'You still do not get it. TEC (Thomas Edwin Castello) is a creation. A MYTH.' He named his ingredients in the same message and described mailing a hundred large packets of supporting material to authors and lecturers who then folded it into their own talks, articles and books. That last sentence is the important one, because it describes the deliberate manufacture of the appearance of independent corroboration: the many later sources that agree about Castello agree because they were seeded from one envelope. This node is therefore not an absence-of-record node and should never be rebuilt as one. Absence of record is what a board writes when it has looked and found nothing; here the author has spoken. The separate checks that were made are consistent with the confession and add nothing to it: John Greenewald, publishing on 1 April 2016, states 'There is no evidence that I have found, that shows that Thomas Costello even exists', and demonstrates that the single most-circulated piece of physical evidence attached to the name, a photograph of bodies in a chamber, is a frame from the 2000 film The 6th Day. One point of honesty about the sourcing: the confession reaches this board at second hand. It was read as reproduced on Norio Hayakawa's site, quoting Gorightly's book, and neither the email nor the book was opened. That is why the confession claim is graded Tier 2 rather than Tier 1, and it is the single item in this cluster most worth upgrading. A further negative recorded by Hayakawa in 2016, that an 'alleged' retired Air Force colonel told him no such person was ever employed at Dulce, is anonymous, is bracketed in quotation marks by Hayakawa himself, and is carried at Tier 3 so that nobody later mistakes it for a check. No jurisdiction, employer of record, date of birth or date of death has ever been attached to the name, which means no records search is even formulable: the claim is built so as to be unfalsifiable by records, and only its author could ever have settled it.

Custody proximity 0, access 0 and disclosure role 0 because a fabricated persona holds no axis of its own: every axis value here belongs to Tal Levesque, who is built separately and carries the disclosure role. The node is retained rather than deleted because the fabrication is itself the finding, and because deleting it would leave the claims that cite him floating with no place to record what happened to them.

people.label: Philip Schneider
people.sub: Lecturer of 1995 who claimed to have helped build the Dulce facility and to have survived a 1979 firefight there; no employment by anyone was ever documented
people.narrative: Philip Schneider supplied every specific number in the modern Dulce claim and none of them can be traced past him. In a lecture at Post Falls, Idaho on 8 May 1995 he said he had been 'involved in building an addition to the deep underground military base at Dulce', that his job was 'to go down the holes and check the rock samples, and recommend the explosive[s]', that the base 'goes down seven levels and over 2.5 miles deep', and that in a cavern there he shot two aliens, after which the thirty people already underground and about forty more who came down were killed. He arrived late: Norio Hayakawa's chronology places him outside the initial rumours entirely and dates his emergence to 1995, when the Dulce story was already about fifteen years old. WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED IS RECORDED HERE AND NOT ONLY IN THE GAPS. No employment of Philip Schneider by anybody, ever, was documented by this board: no employer record, no contract, no clearance record, no payroll. The attribution to Morrison Knudsen, the Corps of Engineers and the Navy rests on a contributor-written biography attached to his Find a Grave memorial and on his own lectures, and a contributor-written memorial biography is not a record of employment. His death is likewise unresolved: the memorial record gives 11 January 1996 in Clackamas County, Oregon, while the date in circulation, tied to the discovery of the body, is 17 January 1996, and NO DEATH CERTIFICATE, MEDICAL EXAMINER'S REPORT OR POLICE REPORT WAS OPENED. The suicide ruling, the ligature and his former wife's letter contesting the finding are all in circulation and none of it is carried as a claim here. The one genuinely documented element of the Schneider story is his father: Captain Otto Oscar Schneider, US Navy, 22 January 1906 to 13 May 1993, on a Find a Grave memorial originally created by the US Veterans Affairs Office. The rank and the dates are real; the narrative attached to the same page, a captured U-boat commander repatriated into US Naval Intelligence, Operation Crossroads and the Philadelphia Experiment, is contributor prose and none of it is asserted. It matters only because Philip Schneider's own claim leaned on his father's standing, and the standing is real while the stories about it are not documented by anything opened here.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C is proximity, not credibility. Custody proximity 0 because no opened record places him in contact with any material or any facility. Access 0 because the board does not score A on a claimed clearance and no clearance, contract or employment of his is documented anywhere in the opened record; this is the axis that carries the whole weight of the node's problem. Disclosure role 3 because his entire documented function is a 1995 lecture series whose content became the specification of the Dulce claim. The tier says where to look, not what is true, and here what a later pass should look for is a personnel or contract record that either exists or does not.

people.label: Milton William Cooper
people.sub: Broadcaster and author who carried the alien-bases-under-reservations frame to a mass audience from 1989; his 1989 paper never names Dulce
people.narrative: Milton William Cooper is a propagation node and the board should be precise about what he propagated, because the usual account overstates it. His paper 'The Secret Government', dated on its own first page 23 May 1989 and updated 21 November 1990, delivered at the MUFON symposium in Las Vegas on 2 July 1989 and later absorbed into his 1991 book Behold a Pale Horse, was extracted and searched in full for this cluster. It contains the frame: 'It was agreed that bases would be constructed underground for the use of the alien nation and that two bases would be constructed for the joint use of the alien nation and the United States Government...These alien bases would be constructed under Indian reservations in the Four Corners area of Utah, Colorado, New Mexico and Arizona, and one would be constructed in an area known as Dreamland.' IT DOES NOT CONTAIN THE WORD DULCE. The string occurs zero times in forty-nine pages. A count is checkable and an adjective is not, which is why the number is carried in the claim rather than a characterisation. Cooper's edge to the hub is therefore Tier 3 frame-propagation and nothing stronger. Two further things belong on the node. First, he graded his own document: after describing his sources as top secret material seen between 1970 and 1973 as a member of the Intelligence Briefing Team of the Commander in Chief of the Pacific Fleet, plus sources he could not divulge and 'published sources which I cannot vouch for', he writes that 'this chapter must be termed a hypothesis'. The board should use the author's own grade. Second, the same document independently corroborates one element of the Kirtland affair: Cooper writes that Linda Moulton Howe 'confided to me that Sgt. Richard Doty of the Counterintelligence Division of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations had taken her into the Intelligence office at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico and showed her the exact same documents that I had seen'. That corroborates that Howe was telling the story by 1989 to a third party. It corroborates nothing about the documents themselves.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C is proximity to the programme and not credibility. Custody proximity 0 because nothing places him near any material; his own account of having read documents in 1970 to 1973 is an assertion and the board does not score custody on an assertion. Access 0 for the same reason: a claimed briefing-team role with no opened service record scores zero on an axis that measures documented access. Disclosure role 3 because his documented function, from the 1989 symposium paper through the 1991 book and the broadcast years, was mass publication. The node is in the media cluster rather than the witness cluster because what is documented about him is distribution, not testimony.

entities.label: Project Gasbuggy, 10 December 1967

entities.desc: Project Gasbuggy is the best counter-explanation artefact in the Dulce cluster, and it is a government fact sheet rather than an argument. On 10 December 1967 the US Atomic Energy Commission detonated a 29-kiloton-yield nuclear device in the emplacement well GB-E at a depth of 4,227 feet, in an attempt to stimulate natural gas production from the overlying Pictured Cliffs Formation. It was the first natural-gas reservoir stimulation experiment in the Plowshare programme, jointly sponsored by the AEC, the Department of the Interior and the El Paso Natural Gas Company. The detonation vaporised rock, produced a cavity, and left a rubble-filled collapse chimney as the overlying rock fell into the void. A reentry well, GB-ER, was drilled into the chimney and contaminated gas was produced and flared through five production tests between July 1968 and October 1969, yielding 213 million cubic feet of natural gas that still carried measurable radioactive constituents and a significantly lower heat value than expected. In 1976 it was decided that no further testing would be conducted. The AEC decommissioned and demobilised the site in 1978, injecting liquid radioactive waste into the former cavity and shipping solid radioactive waste to the Nevada Test Site. Soil sampling followed in 1978, 1986, 2000 and 2002; final surface remediation removed 5,562 cubic yards of contaminated soil and was completed in September 2004. A permanent monument, a brass plaque mounted in a concrete base, marks the spot. THE NODE EXISTS TO STATE ADJACENCY AND PRECEDENCE, NOT CAUSATION. Nothing opened by this board demonstrates that Gasbuggy generated the Dulce rumour, and the dated chronology of the cluster's originators does not say so either. What it establishes is that the United States government did a large, secret, radioactive thing in the ground twelve miles from Dulce in the decade before the rumour began, and then returned to that ground for the next forty years.

Underground? in Dulce?' of 18 January 2009, returned connection refused and HTTP 404 on 19 September 2026, and web.archive.org is unavailable to this session. The widely repeated formulation that the Nation has no official position, and remarks attributed to a public-relations staffer named Merlin Cassador, are NOT asserted anywhere in this build and no edge rests on them. The only tribal official whose words were opened is Legislative Council President Ty Vicenti, quoted in a May 2016 feature issuing a tourism welcome and neither asserting nor denying a base. A sovereign nation whose land is the subject of the claim has not, so far as this session could open, been asked on the record.
gaps.wouldClose: Any of the three 2009 Albuquerque Journal pieces via a non-refusing host; the Chacon article of 8 May 2016, 'A town of true believers'; or a statement obtained directly from the Jicarilla Apache Nation.

gaps.text: THE LOAD-BEARING ITEM OF THE WHOLE CLUSTER IS READ AT SECOND HAND. Tal Levesque's November 2015 email confessing that Thomas Edwin Castello was his own creation was read as reproduced on Norio Hayakawa's site, quoting Adam Gorightly's book. NEITHER THE EMAIL NOR THE BOOK WAS OPENED. Every claim depending on the confession is therefore capped at Tier 2, including the claims on thomas-castello, tal-levesque, dulce-base and d-disinformation. This is the single highest-value upgrade available in this cluster and the board should not lean harder on the confession than Tier 2 until it is closed.
gaps.wouldClose: A first-hand read of Adam Gorightly, 'Saucers, Spooks and Kooks', Daily Grail Publishing, 2021, ISBN 978-0994617682, or of the email itself.

gaps.text: George Knapp's own written account of his own Doty interview was not opened: six separate Nexstar-family URLs, at mysterywire.com, 8newsnow.com, krqe.com, koin.com, kron4.com and yourcentralvalley.com, all returned HTTP 403 on 19 September 2026. The board has the video's auto-generated caption track and NOT ONE WORD of the article. gaps.wouldClose: A non-403 route to the Mystery Wire article, or a syndicated copy on a non-Nexstar host.

gaps.text: Doty's 321-page New Mexico State Police personnel file is Tier 1 as a release and entirely unread as a document. His AFOSI service dates, rank progression and reason for separation remain undocumented beyond the single 1980 complaint form. Given that this cluster turns on what a self-described disinformation officer did and when, the contents of the one official personnel record anyone has obtained is a conspicuous hole.
gaps.wouldClose: Downloading and reading the 321-page PDF from The Black Vault's document archive.

gaps.text: NO EMPLOYMENT OF PHILIP SCHNEIDER BY ANY EMPLOYER WAS DOCUMENTED BY THIS BOARD: no employer record, no contract, no clearance record, no payroll. The attribution to Morrison Knudsen, the US Army Corps of Engineers and the US Navy rests on a contributor-written biography attached to a Find a Grave memorial and on his own lectures. gaps.text: Philip Schneider's death is used as an argument by the literature and is undocumented here. No death certificate, medical examiner's report or police report was opened. Two dates are in circulation, 11 January 1996 from the memorial record and 17 January 1996 tied to the discovery of the body, and the conflict is unresolved. The suicide ruling, the ligature and the letter attributed to Cynthia Drayer of 23 February 1996 contesting the finding are all in circulation and none of it is carried as a claim.
gaps.wouldClose: The Clackamas County medical examiner's report or the Oregon death certificate.

gaps.text: UFO COVER-UP? LIVE! IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. The artefact was not opened in any form: not the broadcast, not a listing, not a contemporaneous review. Its reported date of 14 October 1988, its producer, its 'Falcon' segment and Doty's reported denial of having been Falcon all rest on search summaries. No node and no claim is proposed for it, and it should be built only after somebody opens the artefact. It belongs in the cluster as the moment the material reached a national audience, which is exactly why building it on summaries would be a mistake.
gaps.wouldClose: A recording of the 14 October 1988 syndicated broadcast, a contemporaneous television listing, or a dated contemporaneous review.

gaps.text: A letter from Bennewitz to Senator Pete Domenici dated 2 December 1981, reportedly referring to a 'Dulce War', would be the earliest dated artefact tying Bennewitz's own hand to the place name and would materially strengthen the origin edge into the hub. It is known only from a citation apparatus; the underlying source was not opened and it is not carried as a claim.
gaps.wouldClose: The letter itself, or a contemporaneous source reproducing it.

gaps.text: The earliest contemporaneous sceptical newspaper treatment identified, 'ETs living in NM? Not likely, investigators say' by Kay Bird and Steve Terrell in The Santa Fe New Mexican, is paywalled at newspapers.com and was not opened. It carries two different dates in the two places that cite it, 1 September and 11 September 1988. Opening it would give the cluster a contemporaneous local negative from 1988, which it currently lacks entirely: every sceptical source in this build is from 2013 or later.
gaps.wouldClose: A newspapers.com subscription read, or a library copy of the Santa Fe New Mexican for September 1988.

The file number, the agent and the observers match exactly in both, so this is a transcription question and not a provenance one, but a primary document with two dates on this board is a defect a later pass should close by reading the image.
gaps.wouldClose: Reading the original scanned complaint form image rather than a text rendering of the page.

gaps.text: Whether Project Gasbuggy has anything causally to do with the Dulce rumour could not be established and is not asserted. It is adjacent in space and prior in time by twelve years, and that is the whole of the finding. The denial edge from gasbuggy-1967 into the hub is typed association for exactly this reason: a real hole in the ground is nobody's act of denial, and a plausible mechanism is not a demonstrated one.
gaps.wouldClose: A dated source showing local knowledge of Gasbuggy feeding into the earliest Dulce reports, or a Bennewitz-era document referring to the detonation.
